changes.before: Keep two choice buttons and their summary synchronized through parent state.
changes.after: Put shared state in a parent so related components agree.

before: Two sibling components may need to agree on one value. Independent copies of that value can drift apart.
Move the shared state to their nearest common parent. Pass the current value down through props.
Pass a callback prop down too. A child calls it to request a change; the parent updates the shared state.
A controlled component gets the important value from props rather than keeping its own competing copy. Not all child state must move up—only the state that needs coordination.
For one selected activity, store one activity name rather than two unrelated Booleans. Comparing each button's label with that name makes exactly one button selected.
The starter lets each button select itself independently, so both can stay selected. Move that decision to App and pass selected and onSelect to Choice.
Click Draw, then Read. The selected button and status must agree every time, including when clicking the already selected button.
after: Sibling components are components beside each other under the same parent. If they need to agree on one value, separate copies can disagree.
Keep the shared state in their nearest common parent. Pass its current value down through props.
Also pass a callback: a function the child can call to request a change. The parent uses it to update the shared state.
The child reads `active` from props instead of keeping another copy. Only move state to the parent when it needs to be shared. Other state can stay in a child.
For a choice between two activities, store one selected activity name. Each button can compare its name with that value to find out whether it is selected.
The starter keeps a separate selected value in each button, so both can stay selected. Put the single choice in `App`. Pass `selected` and `onSelect` to each `Choice`.
Click Draw, then Read, then Read again. Exactly one choice and the summary should agree after every click.

before: Put the shared selected value in App.
Let each Choice receive its selected value and selection callback through props.
after: Keep one selected activity name in App.
Pass each Choice its selected value and onSelect callback.
Run the checks and switch between the buttons.

before: Put the shared selected value in App.
Let each Choice receive its selected value and selection callback through props.
after: Each child should read the shared choice instead of storing a second copy.

before.question: Each sibling stores its own selected Boolean. Both can become selected, but only one should be. What change removes that conflicting state?
choices: Store one selected ID in the common parent and pass values/callbacks down
Add an effect to copy each sibling's state into the other forever
Change both button labels to the same word
before.explanation: One shared selected ID expresses the requirement directly. Each child derives its selected value from that ID, so independent copies cannot disagree.

after.question: Two buttons keep separate selected values, so both can stay selected. What fixes this?
choices: Keep one selected ID in the parent and pass values and callbacks down.
Keep copying each button's state into the other.
Give both buttons the same label.
after.explanation: One selected ID expresses one choice. Both children read it, so their separate copies cannot disagree.

changes.before: Existing dashboard shows shared data; this lesson explicitly teaches lifting competing sibling state and controlled props. Tested through actual button interactions. No effects, context, global store, or duplicated synchronized state needed.
changes.after: This lesson uses parent state and child props to keep one shared choice.

headings: Keep it in the common parent

project.title: Let siblings share one choice
project.task: Keep the two activity buttons and their summary in agreement using one choice stored in App.
project.done_when: Exactly one button is selected, and the summary matches after switching or clicking the same choice again.
